roof_age_underwriting.text: Commercial carriers use ISO CP 10 36 'Limitations on Coverage for Roof Surfacing' (introduced in ISO's 2012 filing) or carrier variants to (1) switch roof surfacing from replacement cost to actual cash value and/or (2) exclude cosmetic wind/hail damage (cosmetic exclusion not approved in every state). 'Aged roof' endorsements commonly convert RCV to ACV at a trigger age of 10, 15 or 20 years depending on carrier/state; some use payment schedules (e.g., 100% at 0-5 yrs, 80% at 6-10 yrs). Documented inspection/maintenance records are viewed favorably at renewal. No Virginia-specific commercial roof-age rule or statute was found; thresholds are carrier-specific. Sources are mostly trade press/broker content retrieved via search extracts (unverified).

code_triggers.text: Virginia enforces the Virginia Uniform Statewide Building Code (USBC): the Virginia Construction Code (VCC, based on the 2021 IBC) and Virginia Existing Building Code (VEBC, based on the 2021 IEBC), with energy provisions based on the 2021 IECC. Re-roofing follows IBC Chapter 15 (Section 1511) as referenced by VEBC: a recover (overlay) is generally not permitted where the existing roof or insulation is water-soaked or deteriorated, or where two or more roof coverings already exist, which forces a full tear-off. On roof replacement the IECC generally requires that above-deck insulation be brought up to current code where the insulation is above the deck, which is a major cost driver (local cost guides cite the DC R-33 requirement; Virginia follows the 2021 IECC commercial table). THESE PROVISIONS ARE SUMMARIZED FROM GENERAL KNOWLEDGE OF THE 2021 I-CODES; the Virginia DHCD and ICC code pages could not be opened in this session and exact section numbers, R-values and Virginia amendments must be verified before use in customer-facing material. No Virginia rule was found that forces full replacement at a fixed % of roof damaged; damage-threshold (e.g., 25%/50%) replacement rules were not verified for Virginia.
